text:
infra-bot: [ALERT] policy-engine detected overly permissive IAM role binding: role"svc-data-processor" allows s3:* and kms:* to federated-principal 'accounts:12345' at 2026-03-20T14:02:03Z

maria (secops): saw this alert, looks like a recent terraform apply in `infra/data-processing` changed the role trust/inline policy. tagging @ajay @lisa

ajay (infra): pulling the tf plan now, give me 2

lisa (eng): if it's a deploy from last night, the pipeline should show who merged. i can check PR history

maria (secops): we should assume potential access until proven otherwise. containment: 1) detach inline policy 2) rotate any IAM creds that might be associated 3) restrict KMS key policy to our account principals 4) enable CloudTrail lookup for the role session tokens

jen (security lead): +1. Prioritize removing s3:* and kms:* perms immediately. Notify compliance about potential data exposure.

ajay (infra): running revoke now, will also create a short-lived deny in IAM identity-based policy to block any pass-through while we investigate

ajay (infra): running command:

```
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name svc-data-processor --policy-name temp-deny-all --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"*","Resource":"*"}]}'
```

infra-bot: deploy started: revoke-policy-job (job-id: dq3f)

lisa (eng): saw the pipeline: PR #4822 merged 03/19 by user @service-account-ci. PR changed `modules/processing/iam.tf` to add wide permissions for backwards compat.

maria (secops): good find. Ask CI owner to provide why. Meanwhile, ajay confirm if any active sessions were issued under that role in last 24h

ajay (infra): querying CloudTrail:

```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/svc-data-processor --start-time 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-20T14:00:00Z
```

ajay (infra): result: 3 AssumeRole operations at 2026-03-19T21:12:05Z (session from ec2 role), 2026-03-20T01:03:10Z (lambda), 2026-03-20T09:45:02Z (federated). Need to rotate any long-lived creds used by those principals

maria (secops): mark those sessions as potentially compromised. Add to incident ticket. Changing KMS key policy now to remove wildcard and set explicit principal list.

ajay (infra): KMS modify:

```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/data-processing --policy file://restricted-kms-policy.json
```

maria (secops): also set S3 bucket ACL and bucket policy to deny any requests not from our account (quick containment):

```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket data-prod-exports --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:*","Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::data-prod-exports","arn:aws:s3:::data-prod-exports/*"],"Condition":{"StringNotEquals":{"aws:PrincipalAccount":"111122223333"}}}]}'
```

lisa (eng): applying terraform rollback for that module and opening revert PR to remove the wide permissions. tagging @service-account-ci owner to explain rollback timeline

deploy-bot: revert PR #4828 opened by infra-bot for modules/processing

compliance: please cc legal if we confirm data pulled out of bucket. do we have object-level access logs?

maria (secops): CloudTrail shows GetObject calls for that bucket by the federated principal at 2026-03-20T09:46:00Z for ~12 objects. We need to determine content sensitivity.

lisa (eng): running a quick object inventory to check keys accessed and last modified. will post results in 10m

ajay (infra): revoked the temp-deny policy and replaced role with a locked-down policy that only allows necessary s3:GetObject for specific prefixes and kms:Encrypt/Decrypt only by internal services. recorded change in incident ticket #INC-2026-73

maria (secops): rotated the KMS data-processing key (created new key, re-encrypted recent objects, disabled old key schedule). Note: key rotation is heavy — we scheduled re-encryption job and limited window for reads while rewrap completes.

jen (security lead): timeline looks like: 03/19 PR introduced permissive role, 03/20 detection by policy-engine at 14:02, containment actions (role lock, KMS restrict, bucket deny) executed within 30m. We need a postmortem and code-level guardrails.

maria (secops): immediate follow-ups assigned:
- infra: revert PR and add integration test to fail on wildcard privileges in `modules/processing`
- eng: scan service accounts for any other roles with s3:* or kms:*
- compliance: evaluate accessed objects and decide notification requirements
- devex: add policy-engine rule to block merges that introduce iam:* or kms:* wildcard in policies

lisa (eng): I'll create a PR to add a sentinel/opa check in CI and attach to pre-merge checks.

compliance: please provide a list of object keys and the sensitivity classification. if PII, escalate to legal and customer-notify flow.

maria (secops): logging note: we enabled retention for CloudTrail events for 1y and exported relevant logs to locked bucket `sec-logs-2026` with strict KMS policy. Added an audit entry for the role change and the practitioners involved.

ajay (infra): any creds found tied to the federation source have been revoked where possible and credentials for service accounts rotated. asked teams to rotate any environment variables referencing the role

jen (security lead): good work. schedule postmortem for tomorrow 11:00. include owners: @lisa, @ajay, @maria, @compliance. Action items must have due dates.

maria (secops): will draft postmortem and attach evidence: CloudTrail snippets, terraform diff, commands executed, and timeline. publishing to #postmortems after review. :white_check_mark:

lisa (eng): found two other modules with broad kms privileges in a separate repo, opening PRs to lock them down now

maria (secops): closing loop: incident severity set to HIGH due to actual GetObject calls. no evidence of exfil beyond in-account reads but compliance still reviewing. incident ticket updated and will be included in PM

jen (security lead): add a long-term action: centralize iam role templates and enforce least privilege by default. also consider automated key rotation for customer-sensitive KMS keys.

maria (secops): thanks team. keeping thread open for any new findings.
